sentences.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。

translations.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.
translations.idiomatic: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.

sentences.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。

translations.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

sentences.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。

translations.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.
translations.idiomatic: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."

sentences.zh: 何不先謀之！」

translations.literal: Why not plot first!'
translations.idiomatic: Why not plot first!"

sentences.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。

translations.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。

translations.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
translations.idiomatic: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

sentences.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。

translations.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was branded Jia's man.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。

translations.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.

sentences.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。

translations.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: One slip and Lun's head would roll.

sentences.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」

translations.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'
translations.idiomatic: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."

sentences.zh: 倫然之。

translations.literal: Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun assented.

sentences.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。

translations.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.

sentences.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。

translations.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.
translations.idiomatic: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.

sentences.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。

translations.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。

translations.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.

sentences.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。

translations.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.

sentences.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。

translations.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

sentences.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。

translations.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
translations.idiomatic: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

sentences.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。

translations.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.

sentences.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。

translations.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
translations.idiomatic: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.

sentences.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."

sentences.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。

translations.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The court buried him as Guangling prince.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年五月，陽羨縣離裏山大石自立。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Liang, Wufeng 2, fifth month — a great stone at Lili Mountain in Yangxian county stood upright by itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Wufeng 2 under Wu’s Sun Liang, a great stone at Lili Mountain stood upright on its own.

sentences.zh: 案京房《易傳》曰「庶士為天子之祥也」，其說曰：「石立於山同姓，平地異姓。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."

sentences.zh: 干寶以為「孫皓承廢故之家得位，其應也。」

translations.literal: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."

sentences.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。

translations.literal: Others say it signified Sun Xiu's enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Another reading favored Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 孫休永安二年，將守質子群聚嬉戲，有異小兒忽來言曰：「三公鋤，司馬如。」

translations.literal: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我非人，熒惑星也。」

translations.literal: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."

sentences.zh: 言畢上升，仰視若曳一匹練，有頃沒。

translations.literal: Finishing, it rose into the sky; looking up it seemed to trail a bolt of silk; soon it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The apparition shot upward like a comet and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「後四年而蜀亡，六年而魏廢，二十一年而吳平。」

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."

sentences.zh: 於是九服歸晉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Nine Domains returned to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The empire folded back under the Sima house.

sentences.zh: 魏與吳蜀並戰國，「三公鋤，司馬如」之謂也。

translations.literal: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休時，烏程人有得困病，及差，能以響言者，言于此而聞於彼。

translations.literal: Under Wu's Sun Xiu, a man of Wucheng fell deathly ill; after he recovered he could "resounding-speak" — speak here and be heard there.
translations.idiomatic: During Sun Xiu's reign a Wucheng convalescent acquired ventriloquy that carried his voice miles from his lips.

sentences.zh: 自其所聽之，不覺其聲之大也。

translations.literal: From the listener's own place he did not notice the sound as particularly loud.
translations.idiomatic: Beside him it sounded no louder than ordinary speech.

sentences.zh: 自遠聽之，如人對言，不覺聲之自遠來也。

translations.literal: From a distance it was like face-to-face talk; one did not sense that the voice came from far away.
translations.idiomatic: From afar it seemed like conversation at arm's length, with no hint of distant projection.

sentences.zh: 聲之所往，隨其所向，遠者所過十數里。

translations.literal: The sound went wherever he aimed it; those farthest heard it across more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: He could steer the voice through a dozen leagues or more.

sentences.zh: 其鄰人有責息于外，歷年不還，乃假之使為責讓，懼以禍福。

translations.literal: A neighbor had money lent abroad that went unreturned for years; he borrowed the gift to have him deliver rebukes, threatening fortune or calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A creditor used him to haunt a defaulter abroad with ghostly threats of blessing or woe.

sentences.zh: 負物者以為鬼神，即傎倒畀之，其人亦不自知所以然也。

translations.literal: The debtor took it for a spirit, immediately turned everything over in payment; that man also did not know why it happened thus.
translations.idiomatic: The frightened borrower paid in full at once, while the wonder-worker himself hardly grasped the trick.

sentences.zh: 言不從之咎也。

translations.literal: This was a fault arising from words not following their proper course.
translations.idiomatic: The historians filed it under portents of distorted speech.
